title: @plotbunnyfarm replied to your post “If it’s any help to anyone, here’s how the…”:
description:
@plotbunnyfarm replied to your post “If it’s any help to anyone, here’s how the…”:

you have 6 (presumably working) sewing machines, do you use them all? are they set up for different tasks or are they just for the joy of different machines? (said with some admiration, this sounds like a lot of work and knowledge to restore these)

Most of the machine heads are working, but a lot of them still need work of some kind! When more of them are in a usable condition I definitely will use multiple of them, since they’re pretty diverse and have different advantages.

This 30’s or 40’s Singer 15-91 is the first machine I bought, because I needed a sewing machine when I moved out. It’s been my main machine for the past 7 years, and I hadn’t gotten into refurbishing machines then, so this is the only one I bought already refurbished.

This is an old picture, I recently refinished the case and haven’t gotten photos yet!
It’s a good straight stitch machine and I like it. I suppose the motor could probably benefit from being opened up and cleaned, but it’s controlling better than it was before I bought a new pedal a couple years ago.

This is a “Gimbels” branded Japanese clone of a Singer 15, which I bought at a garage sale because it was $20 and sad and needed my help. I cleaned it all up and it works, but the wooden case was too rotten to save, so I need to get some help to build a new one.
It’s very similar to the 15-91, but there are some differences! It’s got a more obvious drop feed than the hidden one on the 15-91, and a slightly lower feed setting for delicate fabrics. There are little spring loaded plugs on all the top oil holes to keep dust out, and a few other minor differences.
Once I get a new case built for it I’ll sew on it and see how I feel about it. I may re-home one of these machines someday, or maybe even both, depending on which machines I end up using most in future. It’s cool that these can share bobbins, but functionally they’re so similar that I don’t need to keep both forever, especially if I end up having a favourite.

I could pop it in the 15-91 case and give it a go now, actually. Maybe I will do that.

The 99k I recently gave to a friend came from the same garage sale, but I was able to fix the case because it was less damaged. Probably stored on a higher shelf in the same damp room.

The reason I chose the Singer 99k to give away was because I have a Singer 185J, which is a later version of the same model!

Like the Gimbels, it works but I have not used it because the case was a wreck and I need to build a new one. (Since it fits in a 99 case I measured that one before gifting it.)

This does have a different advantage. It’s a ¾ size “portable” model, so everything is a bit smaller, including the feed dogs. And WOW do the shorter feed dogs ever make a difference in turning curves! I was amazed by how tightly I could turn without pivoting when I tried out the finished 99k!
Since I love making leaf themed clothing with serrated edges, I will take advantage of this on future leaf projects.

I took some photos of them together before putting the 99k back in its case, to show how the 185J is really just a 99k in green space age pyjamas. I have so many other black machines and am a sucker for that shade of green, so I kept that one.

The 1885 White VS2 works, but the needle size is a bit troublesome. I have a few precious original needles, which are very long, and the closest modern ones I found are round shank and I can’t get them tightened securely enough in the needle clamp.

They would be fine if I could just file a little dent into the needle shanks, but none of my metal files are hard enough. I could lower the needle bar and use industrial needles, but I have so many other machines that I know my main one will never be one that can’t backstitch, so I can just be gentle with the original needles and maybe eventually get flat bits filed on the modern ones.

I would like to use this for patchwork, since that’s something I don’t need to backstitch for. I haven’t done a patchwork project in a while, but I have plans for some.
Even if I don’t use it very often, it’s nice to have in my bedroom, and it came with a lot of provenance. I know who owned it and made her living sewing on it from approximately the 1910’s until 1984, and I’ve looked at some of her diaries in person. (We’re not related, her much younger cousin is a friend of my uncle’s and he gave me the machine. No clue who owned it for the first few decades of its existence.)

Ooooh hot damn! The 1945 Bernina treadle!!! It’s a KL 105, the first model Bernina ever made for the home sewing market, and apparently a very rare find here in Canada.

This was given to me earlier this year and I am SO excited to get to use it. I’ve got the machine head all clean and it’s stitching fine and I have needles that fit, and I’m currently in the process of refurbishing the treadle table. It needs a lot of work but I hope to get it done soon, while the weather is still good for working outdoors.

It’s a rotary treadle with backstitch AND drop feed! What a dream! It’ll be so smooth and quiet!! It’s got markings in METRIC! It also has a darning/embroidery foot, and it came with a specialized darning hoop for socks. It has so much drawer space.

Look at this stitch length adjustor.

I’m keeping this one forever and ever. It’s too early to say, since I haven’t been able to properly use it yet and I have very little experience with treadles, but there’s a distinct possibility that this could become my new main machine.

Ah, the Pfugly Pfaff 360 from 1970. This was my second ever machine, and I bought it for $25 at an estate sale just because I was having trouble with my 15-91 speed control and I wanted a backup.
Once I got home I learned that it was a really good machine, and also that the innards were very gummed up with the hardened remains of an anti-rust protective wax the manufacturers sprayed in there. I got most of it loose, but the side to side motion is still stuck.

It sews, but currently only in a tiny shitty zigzag. I borrowed a tool from my father to take it apart and get it unstuck, but I haven’t done that yet. It is on my list of goals for this year.
It just makes me a bit nervous to mess with machines this new, I worry I’ll break one of the plastic knobs or something. I already snapped the light switch off while putting the lid on :(

Once I do unstick that part it’ll be able to do zigzag, and an assortment of fancy stitches with this nifty stack of cams. All my other machines are straight stitch and I’ve never had a zigzag machine, so that’ll be cool!
I can live just fine without zigzag, but it will be very nice to have it.
It’s also my only machine where the bed folds down to give you a smaller round bit to sew around, and it came with a darning foot, so maybe once it’s unstuck I’ll get around to mending some of my worn out pants inseams.

The cute little Western Electric in the previous post is very new to me, but I’m excited to try it once I get it all cleaned up and fitted with a hand crank. This 1911 book on free motion treadle embroidery blew my mind, and I do want to try that stuff on my Bernina treadle, but I also really want to try it on a hand crank because I suspect it’ll be easier to place the needle precisely.

And the industrial serger! c. 1970s, with a later motor. What a ridiculous stroke of luck. What an absolute steal. Everyone is correct to be jealous.
I’ve done the oil change and cleaned out the dust filter, so all this beast needs now is for me to repaint some markings that have worn off. I don’t count this in the sewing machine number, since it’s a different thing.
I shall have nice clean finished edges in all my pants without having to go across town to use Mama’s serger.

So that’s my current herd!
Getting the machine head all cleaned up is the fun part, and I can do it at home, but the woodworking stuff is a lot harder since I haven’t really got the tools or space for most of it. I need to get some wood for those 2 cases, and then will get Papa to help, since he has a table saw.
The Western Electric case and Bernina table are going to be sanded, patched, and refinished outdoors because I have no garage, and I need to hurry up before it gets too cold.

I’ve done so much work on so many machines that it seems really weird to still have so few that are actually 100% usable, but they’re getting there! Someday I will have multiple in rotation for different tasks!

Also, since you mentioned knowledge, I would like to once again say that I fell into this accidentally just a couple years ago and pretty much all I knew when I started was how to oil and sew on one. But I looked lots of stuff up on the internet, and learned by taking stuff apart and photographing as I go, and there’s always more I’m learning! Every newly acquired gunky machine is a new adventure.

title: ChatGPT in Siri 'Persistently Underperforming,' Says OpenAI
description:
OpenAI saw disappointing results working with Apple to integrate ChatGPT in Siri, according to court documents filed [PDF] in its ongoing legal fight with Elon Musk's company SpaceXAI (xAI at the time the lawsuit was filed).


Apple added ChatGPT to ‌Siri‌ in December 2024, but users had to go through a multistep opt-in process, which added a layer of friction. By January 2025, OpenAI said the integration was "off to a slow start" and the company cut its forecast for the number of incremental logged-in weekly active users that it expected to get from the partnership.

Much of the filing is redacted, but OpenAI said that by the time Musk's companies filed an antitrust lawsuit against Apple and OpenAI, "it was clear that Apple's integration of ChatGPT was dramatically underperforming." In a later section of the filing, OpenAI said again that the Apple integration was "persistently underperforming," leading to a March 2026 conversation between Apple and OpenAI that is redacted.

OpenAI asked Apple for a two-year exclusivity period, but Apple refused. The agreement between the two companies explicitly said the deal was non-exclusive and Apple had the right to "integrate products or services that provide the same or similar functionality as [ChatGPT]." Apple told OpenAI that it planned to integrate one provider and then add more, and it made similar statements publicly when announcing the feature. Apple also signed a deal with Google, and Apple's newest models are based on Gemini.

OpenAI's filing disputes many of the claims in the xAI lawsuit. Musk alleged OpenAI and Apple had an exclusive deal and that the agreement harmed xAI's growth and customer acquisition. OpenAI says the contract proves there was no exclusive deal, and even if there were, xAI can't prove harm because the ChatGPT ‌Siri‌ integration just didn't draw many new ChatGPT users.
Even if the Court assumes that Apple users who elect to use ChatGPT through Apple Intelligence are foreclosed from OpenAI's rivals (which they are not), the amount of foreclosure caused by the Agreement is indisputably de minimis. While Plaintiffs' experts declined to calculate foreclosure shares, OpenAI's expert, Dr. Catherine Tucker, calculated the share of GenAI consumers who accessed ChatGPT through Apple Intelligence across multiple metrics using the same data and market definition relied upon by Plaintiffs' experts. On these assumptions, Dr. Tucker found foreclosure shares of [REDACTED] across all metrics, consistent with OpenAI's internal view that Apple Intelligence saw minimal usage.

Musk's companies dropped their claims against Apple earlier this month, leaving OpenAI as the sole defendant in the lawsuit. OpenAI's filing asks the court to toss out xAI's claims prior to the trial planned for January 2027.

title: Most workers are working on Sundays—here’s why
description:
Nearly three-quarters of workers (74%) work on Sunday, including 21% who work a full or near-full day, according to Owl Labs’ tenth annual State of Hybrid Work report.

The trend is far more common among younger generations, with 76% of Gen Z workers and 62% of millennials saying they often work on Sunday, compared to 34% of baby boomers and 42% of Gen Xers.

The report says AI adoption may partly explain the spread of Sunday work. Nearly two-thirds (62%) of respondents said AI has increased what they’re expected to accomplish in a day, and 46% say it sometimes hinders their productivity.

Another potential culprit is meeting fatigue: 38% of workers said meetings leave them overburdened during the week, citing overly long meetings (45%), too many meetings overall (41%), and too many back-to-back meetings (34%).

Workers are also adopting a more flexible approach to scheduling in general. Nearly two-thirds (61%) expressed interest in “microshifting,” or working in “short, non-linear blocks to manage [their] workday around parenting, health, energy levels, or [their] personal productivity.”

Owl Labs, a Boston-based provider of videoconferencing solutions, surveyed 2,000 full-time knowledge workers in the U.S. on issues related to remote, hybrid, and in-office work.

Overall, the percentage of workers in the office full-time rose from 63% to 65% in 2025, and the percentage on a hybrid schedule fell from 28% to 25%. However, flexible work remains broadly popular: 46% of respondents said they would work a hybrid schedule if they could.

The report also reflects the newfound ubiquity of AI, with 82% of employees saying they use it, including 90% of Gen Z. The share who said they use it daily climbed from 27% to 32% year over year.

The rise of AI has had both benefits and drawbacks. On the positive side, 69% of workers said AI has made them more productive and 66% said it has boosted their confidence. However, 46% said it sometimes hinders their productivity, and another 46% worry AI could make their roles unnecessary.

AI use was more common among managers (92%) than individual contributors (62%).

According to data from the International Vaccine Access Center at the Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health, measles cases have now surpassed the 3,500 mark—a level not seen in 35 years.

Here’s what you need to know about the multiple outbreaks affecting the country, and which areas are currently being hit the hardest.

What’s happened?

According to the Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health, as of September 18, 3,568 measles cases were reported in the United States this year so far.

More worryingly, nearly 10% of those cases—341 of them—occurred in the previous two weeks leading up to September 18.

The figure is nearly 1,300 more than the total U.S. measles cases reported in all of 2025, and a level not seen since 1991, when the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) says measles cases reached 9,643.

Speaking of those CDC numbers, if you look at the agency’s official data up to September 18, you’ll see it differs slightly from the John Hopkins’s data. According to the CDC, measles cases for 2026 in the U.S. stand at 3,471 as of September 18. That’s a discrepancy of 97.

The difference seems to stem from the timeframes and the data the CDC uses to update its official measles dashboard, including, as the Guardian noted, how it registers measles deaths.

The CDC says its dashboard is updated with “only confirmed measles cases notified to CDC as of noon on Thursdays,” while John Hopkins updates its dashboard on Fridays “with intermittent updates as warranted.”

Why is measles surging in the United States?

Regardless of which current tally you go by, there’s no disputing that measles is running rampant in America compared to the historic number of cases going back the last three decades.

Measles was officially declared eradicated in America in 2000, with only dozens to a few hundred cases popping up in most years between 2000 and 2018. But then in 2019, measles cases spiked to more than 1,200, according to CDC data. 

Cases dropped again during the pandemic as social distancing made the spread of the virus harder, but then in 2025 they surged to nearly 2,300, and in 2026, cases now top 3,500.

And it’s not just America. As reported by UNICEF USA last November, measles cases are rising globally.

But why? UNICEF says there are two main culprits: rising vaccine hesitancy and public health funding cuts. Both have accelerated in the U.S. since 2025, when measles cases began skyrocketing in the country.

Mapping measles in the U.S.

Both the CDC and John Hopkins have maps that track the number of measles cases across the country.

The CDC’s most recent map shows that in 2026, measles cases have been reported in all but five states.

The five states with no reported cases are Arkansas, Hawaii, Mississippi, Nevada, and New Hampshire.

But those are the outliers. The map shows that nine states have reported more than 100 cases each, with the top three states reporting more than 500 cases each.

The worst state when it comes to the number of cases is Pennsylvania, where an outbreak is ongoing. That state so far has had 745 cases in 2026. South Carolina comes in second with 670 cases this year, and Utah third with 527 cases.

John Hopkins’s measles tracker map corroborates those state rankings on a year-to-date basis. However, the university also offers another map that covers just the last two-week period, which helps to visualize where outbreaks are currently occurring.

According to that map, for the September 4 to September 18 period, 314 cases have been confirmed, with the majority—193 of them—happening in Pennsylvania. Ohio is the next state with the highest number of cases, at 58. Wisconsin follows in third place with 20 cases.

title: These tropical trees breathe at night to survive drought
description: Some tropical trees have evolved a clever way to survive drought by taking in carbon dioxide at night, allowing them to keep their pores closed during the hot daytime and conserve water. By comparing three Clusia species, researchers discovered that this water-saving form of photosynthesis, known as CAM, did not arise through a single evolutionary change. Instead, ancient genome duplications followed by millions of years of genetic reshuffling produced strikingly different strategies, from strong CAM to stress-triggered and hybrid forms.

title: Between Burning Forests and Utopian Cities: Designing the Climate Transition
description: There is no shortage of ways to imagine what the world will look like after a climate catastrophe. Genres of movies and novels have been built around the question of what happens when contemporary safeguards fail, from dystopian fiction and post-apocalyptic literature to disaster films, graphic novels, and video games. Burning forests, submerged cities, abandoned infrastructure, resource scarcity, and mass displacement are a familiar visual and narrative vocabulary. We have become remarkably fluent in imagining the consequences of a world that fails to respond to climate change.

title: Above the Snowline: 11 Shelters Built at the Limits of Construction
description: There is no harder place to build than a high mountain, and none where a building feels more provisional. From the Andes to the Himalaya to the Alps, high-altitude construction strips architecture back to its most elementary transactions. The rock reads as permanence itself, yet a structure set near the limit of habitation exists in negotiation with almost everything around it: with wind that arrives without obstruction, with a ground too steep and too frozen to excavate, and with everything it needs arriving from far below. What can be carried up, what can be assembled by few hands, and what can sustain itself are some of the terms of the problem.

title: New Mac Mini Has Two Storage Downsides, Including Unremovable SSD
description:
As confirmed by the website "Expand Mac mini," NAND storage in the new Mac mini models with the M6 and M5 Pro chips is soldered to the logic board, whereas the previous models with the M4 and M4 Pro chips have removable storage that can be upgraded.


In other words, the new Mac mini does not support aftermarket storage upgrades.

"Expand Mac mini" offers plug-and-play SSD modules that are functionally equivalent to Apple's proprietary modules, yet hundreds of dollars cheaper. As a result, customers were able to save a significant amount of money by configuring their Mac mini with the minimum 256GB capacity that was available on Apple's online store and later installing a higher-capacity aftermarket module. With the new models, that is no longer possible.

"We will keep looking for an opening, but support for the M6 and M5 Pro now looks unlikely," the "Expand Mac mini" website said, in a blog post.

Mac mini models with the M1 chip and M2/M2 Pro chips also had NAND soldered to the logic board, so the M4/M4 Pro configurations having removable storage has proven to be a one-off exception for now. Apple has not commented on the reversal.

In addition, all new Mac mini configurations with 256GB of storage reportedly have a single NAND chip, rather than a pair of 128GB chips. As a result, 256GB configurations have slower SSD speeds compared to configurations with 512GB of storage or more that do have dual NAND chips, according to AAPL Ch.'s testing with Blackmagic's Disk Speed Test benchmark tool.






















Mac mini Configuration Read Speed Write Speed
M6, 512GB 6,371.5 MB/s 6,577.4 MB/s
M6, 256GB 3,216.8 MB/s 3,000.2 MB/s
M4, 256GB 2,792.5 MB/s 2,014.5 MB/s



The new 256GB model's Disk Speed Test scores were roughly half that of models with 512GB of storage or more. The average customer is unlikely to notice the difference, but power users will appreciate knowing that they need to opt for at least 512GB of storage in order to achieve the fastest SSD speeds possible.

Fortunately, even with 256GB of storage, it appears that the new Mac mini has meaningfully faster SSD speeds compared to the previous 256GB model.

Mac mini models with M2/M2 Pro and 256GB of storage also had a single NAND chip, so the M4/M4 Pro configurations proved to be a one-off exception for this too.

title: People are ‘bricking’ their smartphones on purpose to stop doomscrolling
description:
As personal devices continue to advance, more and more consumers are craving the opposite: a way to dumb down their smartphones to match the simple tech of yesteryear.

According to the latest Pew Research Center survey, over half of American adults (53%) self-identify as spending too much time on their phones, with 1 in 4 adults saying they’re on their smartphones “almost constantly.” Those figures increase among younger demographics, with 70% of Americans ages 18 to 29 saying they spend too much time on their phone and 42% saying they’re nearly constantly using it.

Those who feel like they’re overusing their phones aren’t just sitting idly by. Nearly half of American adults (45%) have tried to cut back on their smartphone usage in the past 12 months—but that’s easier said than done. Only a quarter of those who’d tried to cut back on their smartphone screen time said they felt they were extremely or very successful in doing so. With social media and other popular phone apps notorious for keeping users in a dopamine-fueled feedback loop, it’s no surprise that breaking a smartphone habit might require outside intervention.

That’s why a growing cohort of consumers are fighting fire with fire, turning to a trendy device that forces them to get off their phones and be in the moment.

Meet Brick

In 2023, lifelong friends TJ Driver and Zach Nasgowitz co-founded Brick, a tech company with a flagship product designed to break bad smartphone habits once and for all.

Brick looks unassuming: It’s a small, gray plastic cube just 2 inches long on each side. But it contains near-field communication (NFC) technology that connects to an app on users’ phones, where they can pick and choose which apps they want to block themselves from using.

To enable those blocks, users must tap their phones on the Brick device. To turn them off and access the apps, users have to tap Brick again, adding a physical component that makes all the difference when it comes to screen time.

Though smartphones have built-in features to limit screen time, they mean almost nothing in the face of active addiction to social media. The iPhone’s “Screen Time” limits, for example, can be bypassed with the tap of a button that pops up when you try to access a blocked app.

Brick solves that problem by moving the bypass button into the physical world. Even when Brick is nearby, it adds another hurdle to accessing apps that you want to stop yourself from using. And if you leave Brick at home while you’re out of the house, you’re guaranteed to stop yourself from doomscrolling, checking social media, or doing any other activity that would distract from your real-world tasks.

According to an internal survey of more than 3,500 customers, Brick says 95% of its users say they feel less distracted, 93% say they’re more focused, and 99% report reduced screen time. The Brick device retails for $59.

Since its release in 2023, Brick has blown up in popularity. Though the company is tight-lipped on its sales figures, its app is downloaded tens of thousands of times each month according to data from digital market intelligence company Similarweb.

Making “bricks” from scratch

Though Brick is the leader in the dumbing-down space, some savvy social media users have found ways to recreate its effects with easily accessible materials.

Combining NFC stickers (which go for less than $10 on online marketplaces) and free apps like Foqos, some users are DIY-ing their own Brick-esque devices, customized to their aesthetics. One TikTok user showed the process of turning a small wooden appliqué into her own take on an app-blocker, garnering 13,000 likes. Another user made what she called “the pebble” by surrounding an NFC tag with air-dry clay and paint.

Brick, meanwhile, has started selling cases to make its simple gray devices more aesthetically pleasing.

title: Mary Cassatt: The Impressionist Who Painted The Mind
description:
I always learn so much from Evan Puschak’s videos about art. In this one, he takes a look at the work of Mary Cassatt, who, unlike many of her male peers, used the flattened perspective of Impressionism to reveal the thoughts and feelings of her subjects.

Like Manet, she’s dispensing with traditional modeling and perspective. In fact, her choice of a mirror as background is a brilliant way to literally and figuratively foreground the deceptive nature of perspective. Like Degas, she’s exploring the changing effects of artificial light on flesh and fabric. And she’s experimenting with off-kilter viewing angles.

But Cassat isn’t just adopting these techniques for the sake of it. She’s putting them to work in service of her deeper interest in psychology. She realizes that by not allowing the viewer to get drawn into the narrative space opened up by perspective, this new style of painting actually makes it possible to depict the subtle psychology of everyday life, a psychology uncontaminated by allegory or sentimentality. The trick was to combine the immediacy of Manet’s methods with a meticulous observation of posture, gesture, expression, and activity.

title: “Slip, Slop, Slap, Seek, Slide”: What about Nicotinamide … for Skin Cancer Prevention?
description:
“Slip, Slop, Slap, Seek, Slide”: What about Nicotinamide … for Skin Cancer Prevention? hmarshall@ebsco.com Tue, 09/22/2026 - 13:29 Skin cancer remains one of the most common cancers worldwide, and prevention strategies are critical. This article explores nicotinamide, a novel approach to skin cancer prevention.
No
Alaina James, MD, PhD
2026-09-22T18:00:00

Skin cancer remains one of the most common cancers worldwide, and prevention strategies are critical. While sun protection – including broad-spectrum sunscreen, protective clothing, and seeking shade – remains the cornerstone of prevention, emerging evidence suggests that oral nicotinamide, a form of vitamin B3, may offer additional protection against certain skin cancers.

The Mechanism of Action: Nicotinamide and its Effects on Skin

Nicotinamide (also known as niacinamide) is the amide form of vitamin B3 and is structurally and functionally different from niacin, the acid form. Both forms support cellular health by serving as a precursor to NAD⁺, a critical coenzyme involved in energy metabolism and DNA repair. Unlike niacin, nicotinamide does not cause flushing or significantly decrease cholesterol levels, making it a better tolerated option for routine use.  However, nicotinamide should be avoided in people with liver disease, severe hepatic dysfunction, active peptic ulcer disease, or known hypersensitivity.

The proposed biologic mechanisms of nicotinamide for skin protection include:

  • Enhanced DNA repair following UV-induced damage
  • Improved cellular energy metabolism through NAD⁺ pathways
  • Reduced UV-induced immunosuppression

Together, these effects may help explain observed reductions in non-melanoma skin cancer risk.

The Evidence: Nicotinamide and Skin Cancer Prevention 

A large retrospective cohort study of more than 33 thousand U.S. veterans examined the effects of nicotinamide at a dose of 500 mg twice daily for more than 30 days. Among the 12,287 patients who received nicotinamide compared with 21,479 matched controls, there was a 14 percent overall reduction in skin cancer risk. 

Most notably, those who began nicotinamide after their first skin cancer diagnosis had an approximate 54 percent risk reduction, with the strongest effects seen for both squamous cell carcinoma and basal cell carcinoma.

These results, while encouraging, come with limitations. The study cohort was predominantly homogeneous, and no protective effect was observed in people with solid organ transplant or other forms of immunosuppression. Further randomized trials in more diverse populations are essential to determine the broader applicability of nicotinamide in clinical practice.

Clinical Takeaways For Skin Cancer Prevention

While nicotinamide may help prevent basal cell carcinoma and cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma, the essentials of sun protection remain unchanged. In addition to consulting your health care team to check any suspicious skin lesion and regular skin checks, the Australian Cancer Council reminds the global community to “Slip, Slop, Slap, Seek, Slide” by:

  • Slipping on sun-protective clothing
  • Slopping on broad-spectrum SPF 30+ sunscreen (reapplied every two hours)
  • Slapping on a wide-brimmed hat
  • Seeking shade
  • Sliding on wraparound sunglasses

Given its favorable safety profile and low cost, oral nicotinamide may be considered another preventive strategy for people at high-risk for skin cancer, particularly those with a history of non-melanoma skin cancer.

The Bottom Line For Nicotinamide

Nicotinamide is a promising, well-tolerated option that could complement established prevention strategies. Further research is needed before widespread adoption.

title: Oakland, California trip report
description:
Yesterday on this blog we highlighted Piedmont, California, which is 0.8% Black and 3.8% Latinx. Today we look at diversity-is-our-strength Oakland.

Folks in Oakland seem to have a lot more sex. “Cheated On? freeSTDcheck.org”:

Oakland is a center for Rainbow-first retail. Before one can spend $6 on a coffee, for example, one must walk underneath the sacred flag:

Who are the customers for $6 coffees? Quite a few undocumented immigrants, it seems, because the coffee shop is officially a place where migrant customers are safe from ICE thugs. (I didn’t see a bathroom for customers, so I’m not sure just how long a noble undocumented migrant could stay, as a purely practical matter.)

What passion goes hand-in-glove with Rainbow Flag worship? Pro-Hamas advocacy. The windows next to the door of Walden Pond Books.

What’s in the bookstore? Books celebrating a Hamas-/Palestinian Islamic Jihad-ruled “Free Palestine” with a Rainbow Flag in the background:

Detail:

Who among us is obstructing the glorious day when Free Palestine arrives? If we could only “catch a fascist” we, and our Palestinian brothers, sisters, and binary-resisters, might yet be okay.

What language would people speak in Free Palestine? “Queer Arabic”:

Were they any tutorials available on how to be queer? So glad that you asked! You can learn how to cook “Queer Food” from Queers at the Table and put in on a table that is an example of Queer X Design.

How different are readers’ tastes in California vs. the national average? Prominently featured Queers at the Table has just two Amazon reviews is “#753,447 in Books”. Queer X Design is significantly more popular: “#343,353 in Books”.

A queer hijabi Muslim immigrant survives her coming-of-age by drawing strength and hope from stories in the Quran … Through personal experiences, Lamya H navigates the complexities of gender, sexuality and faith as a queer, nonbinary Muslim.

What kind of people want to pay full price for books in the English language? Undocumented migrants who will presumably be shielded from ICE by the merchant:

What if you’re planning to head up the hill to Piedmont and need to agitate against the construction of affordable housing? You can prep by reading Golden Gates, regarding the “housing crisis” that in no conceivable way could have been caused by importing at least 70 million humans (more than the current population of France), mostly low-skill, over the past 50 years.

Criminals don’t tend to either Black or Latinx, but the bookstore says that you should buy “Books on Black, Latinx … history and culture” for people who are current incarcerated.

title: Fire amoeba breaks complex-life heat tolerance record at 63°C
description:
Scientists have identified a new amoeba, Incendiamoeba cascadensis, that can eat, move and reproduce in water as hot as 63°C (145°F) at California’s Lassen Volcanic National Park, setting a record for the highest temperature known to support eukaryotic reproduction. The NASA-supported study, published in Cell on Sept. 22, found that the organism remains active at about 64°C and can recover after five minutes at 70°C, although exposure to 80°C proved fatal [phys.org#1][nasa.gov#1][livescience.com#1][sciencenews.org#1].

The finding challenges the previous 60°C upper limit for eukaryotic growth and reproduction, based on the heat sensitivity of proteins and other complex cellular structures. Researchers said the amoeba withstands the heat by changing shape and forming a protective outer layer; genetic analysis also identified genes associated with repairing heat-damaged proteins [nasa.gov#1][science.org#1][orf.at#1]. The work is relevant to astrobiology because scientists use extreme environments on Earth to assess where complex life might survive on Mars and other worlds [nasa.gov#1][npr.org#1].

title: As president of Botswana, I know how we can make malaria a memory in Africa | Duma Gideon Boko
description:
The disease is soaring as funding is cut. African nations are plugging the gap but they need help with the transition

Botswana nearly defeated malaria. In 2024, we recorded just 290 cases and one death. Through our elimination efforts, many of our districts had seen no local malaria cases since 2010. Then, as is unfortunately the nature of malaria, it came back.

In the first 23 weeks of 2025 we recorded 2,223 cases and 11 deaths. The disease reached places where previously there was no malaria. We were not alone. Namibia recorded more than 95,000 cases in 2025, and Zimbabwe more than 156,000, according to government figures.

title: Swallowable paper battery powers medical devices in pigs
description:
Researchers developed a small battery made from magnesium and molybdenum trioxide that can be swallowed to power temporary medical devices inside the gastrointestinal tract. In pig tests, the battery produced a peak voltage of 1.84 volts and operated for up to three days, powering a wireless throat tag that transmitted to a receiver 1.5 metres away and a capsule that electrically stimulated the stomach for 20 minutes [scimex.org#1][livescience.com#1].

The battery uses materials intended to break down in the body after use, potentially removing the need to retrieve conventional batteries from temporary ingestible devices. The study remains at an early animal-testing stage: researchers tested a small number of pigs, and the circuit board did not fully degrade but passed in the animals' feces [scimex.org#1]. MIT said the researchers built two versions—a 7.5-millimetre disc and a 24-millimetre rectangular bar—for possible drug-delivery, sensing and other applications [mit.edu#1].

title: Roman Baths of Slovenia (Rimski Terma) in Slovenia
description:
In a valley surrounded by forested mountains is a mineral spring and baths in use since the Roman Empire. The baths were frequented by soldiers and royalty who wanted to take advantage of its purported healing properties. The land around the baths feature historical walking paths lined with trees donated to the area by high society visitors such by Victoria of Prussia who gifted a giant sequoia.

The baths traverse a large, quiet space inside into an outside area with a stunning view. In the area are two smaller hot water mineral baths  equipped with jets and a sprawling space with chairs and umbrellas for outdoor lounging.

In full, the complex is a hiking area, hotel, spa, restaurant, bar, and cafe with more spaces for events. Don't forget to fill your water bottle from the mineral spring and take note of the Latin phrases around the building and baths.

That same threshold is known to trigger jets from much smaller black holes in the Milky Way.

title: Should you buy a Mac mini now? M6 vs M5 Pro buying advice
description:
Macworld

It’s a good time to buy a Mac mini. Apple announced the new M6 and M5 Pro Mac mini on August 25, with shipping from September 22. With another significant update unlikely soon, there is little reason to wait if you need a compact desktop Mac.

For most buyers, we recommend the M6 Mac mini. Starting at $899/£899 – up from $599 for the M4 generation – it offers improved performance for everyday work, coding and creative tasks. It is particularly appealing if you already own a monitor, keyboard and mouse, or are replacing an Intel Mac or early Apple silicon model.

The M5 Pro Mac mini is aimed at more demanding users. Its faster CPU and GPU, Thunderbolt 5, greater memory bandwidth and support for up to 64GB of unified memory make it better for professional creative work, development and larger local AI models. However, prices start at $1,699/£1,699 and rise quickly with upgrades.

This guide explains whether to buy now, which model to choose, how much to pay, and the alternatives, drawbacks and refurbished options to consider.

Should you buy a Mac mini now?

There are reasons to wait. Discounts are likely to improve in the months after launch, particularly around Prime Day in October and Black Friday in November, and more refurbished or discounted M4 models may appear as buyers upgrade. If you’re happy with your current Mac, want to see independent benchmarks first or simply want the lowest possible price, there is no need to rush.

You may prefer not to risk waiting. A global memory shortage contributed to long delivery times and limited availability for the previous generation, and similar supply constraints could affect the new models. The higher cost of memory and other components has also contributed to the Mac mini’s substantial price increase.

Buy Mac mini now if:

  • You need a Mac mini now and want the latest model.
  • You’re replacing an Intel Mac or an older Apple silicon Mac.
  • You want a powerful compact desktop for everyday, office, development or creative work.
  • The $899/£899 M6 Mac mini provides all the performance you need.

Consider M5 Pro if:

  • You need more than 32GB of unified memory.
  • You run demanding professional creative or development workloads.
  • You want to run larger local AI or LLM workloads.
  • You need Thunderbolt 5 or substantially greater memory bandwidth.

Wait if:

  • You want to see independent benchmarks of the new models.
  • You’re hoping for discounts around Prime Day or Black Friday.
  • Your current Mac still meets your needs.
  • You don’t need a new Mac urgently and want to see whether prices fall.

Consider refurbished if:

  • You can find an M4 Mac mini at a significant discount.
  • You want the best value rather than the newest chip.
  • An Apple-refurbished M4 or M4 Pro configuration meets your memory and storage needs.
  • You’re comfortable waiting for refurbished M6 or M5 Pro stock to appear.

Apple Mac mini (M6, 2026)

Price When Reviewed: $899
Best Prices Today: $879.99 at Amazon | $899 at Apple

Apple Mac mini (M5 Pro, 2026)

Price When Reviewed: $1,699
Best Prices Today: $1,669.99 at Amazon | $1699 at Apple

Which Mac mini to buy: M6 or M5 Pro?

Simon Jary / Foundry

The Mac mini lineup has changed significantly in 2026, with Apple introducing the M6 and M5 Pro models in August. The choice between them comes down to your workload and budget, as they serve very different audiences despite sharing the same compact design.

Apple sells two Mac mini models, both announced on August 25 and shipping from September 22, 2026:

Mac mini (M6) — starts at $899 / £899

  • 12-core CPU, 12-core GPU
  • 16GB unified memory (up to 32GB)
  • Up to 2TB SSD
  • Thunderbolt 4 (three ports), two front USB-C ports, HDMI, 2.5Gb Ethernet (10Gb Ethernet optional)
  • Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6 and Thread
  • Supports up to three displays (two 6K + one 5K)

Mac mini (M5 Pro) — starts at $1,699 / £1,699

  • 15-core CPU, 16-core GPU (upgradeable to 18-core CPU, 20-core GPU for +$200)
  • 24GB unified memory (up to 64GB)
  • Up to 8TB SSD
  • Thunderbolt 5 (three ports), two front USB-C ports, HDMI, 2.5Gb Ethernet (10Gb Ethernet optional)
  • Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6 and Thread
  • Supports up to three 6K displays

Despite the “M5” name being a generation older than “M6,” the M5 Pro is the more powerful chip — it has more CPU and GPU cores, substantially greater memory bandwidth – 307GB/s, compared with 153GB/s or 170GB/s for the M6, depending on the memory configuration, and supports far more unified memory.

Choose the M6 Mac mini if:

  • You don’t need more than 32GB of unified memory (RAM).
  • You need a compact, powerful desktop for everyday use – web browsing, office work, photo editing, coding, and general productivity.
  • You’re a student or budget-conscious buyer looking for the best-value option for home offices, school or office use. Education pricing brings the starting price down to $799.
  • You already own a monitor, keyboard, and mouse.
  • You don’t need the extra performance or connectivity of the M5 Pro model.

Choose the M5 Pro Mac mini if:

  • You’re a developer, video editor, 3D artist, musician, or researcher who needs sustained performance for demanding workloads.
  • You want to run larger local AI models. The M5 Pro’s higher memory ceiling and much greater memory bandwidth make it better suited to heavier LLM workloads than the M6. If local AI is a priority, choose your memory carefully because it cannot be upgraded later.
  • You need Thunderbolt 5 for faster external storage, high-bandwidth peripherals or professional video workflows.
  • You regularly work with heavy 3D rendering, high-end video production, large codebases or scientific workloads.
  • You need more than 32GB of unified memory.

How much should you pay for Mac mini?

  • M6 Mac mini, starting at $899.
  • M5 Pro Mac mini, starting at $1,699.

Since the August 2026 update, the Mac mini is no longer the budget Mac it once was. The M6 model starts at $899, $300 more than the $599 starting price of the M4 generation.

For most people, the $899 M6 Mac mini is the model to buy. It offers more than enough performance for everyday work, browsing, media and general productivity, although the standard 16GB of unified memory and 256GB SSD may feel limiting if you plan to keep it for several years.

If you need more demanding performance for creative work, development or running local AI models, the M5 Pro Mac mini starts at $1,699. Configurations with more memory and storage can quickly push the price towards $3,000, so it only makes sense if you genuinely need that extra performance.

Be cautious about spending heavily on Apple’s storage upgrades. External SSDs and Mac mini hubs with NVMe storage can provide considerably more capacity for less money.

For most buyers, we recommend spending around $899 on the M6 Mac mini. Move up to the M5 Pro only if you need its extra processing power or significantly more memory.

Discounts are likely to appear at Amazon and other resellers over time, particularly around Prime Day in October and Black Friday in November. For now, the best bargain may be a discounted M4 Mac mini, although remaining stock is likely to be limited.

Find Apple on Amazon U.S.

Find Apple on Amazon U.K.

Students can save $100 through Apple’s Education Store, reducing the M6 Mac mini to $799 and the M5 Pro model to $1,599. Apple’s Refurbished Store is another way to save, although it may be some time before the new M6 and M5 Pro models appear there. Read: How to get an Apple student discount at Apple’s Education Store and Should you buy a refurbished Mac.

Reasons to buy a Mac mini

Foundry

Excellent value: The price has gone up, but the Mac mini remains one of the most versatile and cost-effective ways to enter the macOS ecosystem. Even at the new starting price of $899, the Mac mini still delivers excellent performance per dollar. That balance of price, power, and efficiency is one of the main reasons for the desktop’s growing popularity. It also offers access to professional-grade performance for significantly less cash than a similarly specced MacBook Pro.

Long software support window: The M6 and M5 Pro Mac mini will have a long usable lifespan and will receive many years of macOS updates and security support.

Compact desktop footprint: The Mac mini’s ultra-compact 5-inch square design makes it one of the most space-efficient desktop computers available. It fits easily under monitors, in small offices, or in minimalist workstation setups. Its compact form factor also makes it particularly attractive for server racks, home labs, and multi-machine deployments. 

Retail discounts and refurbished deals: Despite already offering strong value at full price, the Mac mini is occasionally discounted by third-party retailers. If you can find a Mac mini deal – even on a M4 model with a higher-memory configuration – we recommend taking advantage of it. The Apple Refurbished Store can offer even better value, assuming stock is available. In the past, we have seen the M4 Mac mini discounted by around $100/£100, while M4 Pro models have dropped by approximately $200/£210. If deals like these reappear, they are likely worth considering.

Reasons not to buy Mac mini

The price has gone up significantly: The Mac mini was once the undisputed budget Mac, but that is much harder to say now. The entry-level model has risen sharply in price, making it less compelling for buyers primarily looking for the cheapest way into the Mac ecosystem. At $899, the latest Mac mini is still less expensive than a MacBook or iMac, but it no longer feels like the bargain it once was.

You need to buy your own peripherals: The Mac mini is a “BYODKM” – Bring Your Own Display, Keyboard and Mouse – computer. That’s central to its appeal if you already own those accessories, but it can add substantially to the cost if you don’t. Unlike an iMac or MacBook, the Mac mini doesn’t include a display, keyboard or mouse. Buying all three can easily add hundreds of dollars to the overall price. The latest models also lack USB-A ports, so you may need adapters or a hub if you still use older accessories.

It’s not portable: The Mac mini is a desktop computer, so it isn’t suitable if you need to work in different locations. You can’t easily take it to a lecture, meeting or coffee shop in the way you can a MacBook. For students, frequent travellers or anyone who regularly works away from a desk, a laptop is likely to be the better choice.

You can’t upgrade it later: You need to choose your memory and storage carefully when you buy because neither can be upgraded afterwards. Apple’s build-to-order memory and storage upgrades can also be expensive, particularly once you start moving beyond the base configuration. This can quickly push the Mac mini into MacBook Pro or Mac Studio territory. Storage is less of a concern because inexpensive external SSDs and Mac mini hubs with NVMe storage can add capacity later, but there is no equivalent workaround for unified memory.

Availability could be limited: New Mac launches can sometimes bring longer delivery times for popular configurations, particularly higher-memory or build-to-order models. The M6 and M5 Pro Mac mini may suffer significant shortages due to their popularity and the shortage of components and memory.

It’s not ideal for every AI workload: Apple is increasingly positioning its Macs for AI workloads, with the M6 GPU’s Neural Accelerators and dual 16-core Neural Engine, but as our colleagues at PCWorld explain, the Mac mini has some limitations if running large local models is your main priority. The standard M6 Mac mini tops out at 32GB of unified memory, which may be restrictive for particularly large local models. The M5 Pro model offers more memory, but higher-spec configurations become expensive quickly. There is also no support for Nvidia’s CUDA platform. Many professional AI and machine-learning tools are optimized around CUDA and Nvidia GPUs, so a Windows or Linux PC with a suitable Nvidia graphics card may be faster or better supported for some workloads. For general Apple Intelligence features and lighter local AI use, however, this shouldn’t be a concern.

What to avoid when buying a Mac mini

IDG

Intel: Avoid Intel-powered Mac mini models – when shopping for a refurbished Mac mini, prioritize models with Apple Silicon (M-series chips). 

Low RAM: We advise avoiding 8GB RAM models if possible, as newer generations now start with 16GB as the base standard. 

Check status: Check whether an older model is classified as vintage or obsolete. Service for vintage Macs depends on parts availability, while Apple generally ends hardware service for obsolete Macs. See: How long do Macs last.

Is Mac mini right for you?

Is the Mac mini the best choice for you? There are a number of trade-offs to consider. 

Who is the Mac mini best for?

Mac mini vs Mac Studio: Which should you buy?

Thomas Bergbold

The choice between the Mac mini and the Mac Studio largely comes down to whether you prioritize value or maximum performance.

The Mac mini offers some of the best value in Apple’s desktop lineup. Even the standard M6 model delivers impressive performance for everyday computing, creative work, software development, and local AI tasks, while the M5 Pro configuration provides power for more demanding workloads.

The Mac Studio is designed for users who need workstation-class performance. Following the discontinuation of the Mac Pro, it is now effectively Apple’s most powerful desktop. Starting at $2,499/£2,499 for the M5 Max configuration, the Mac Studio also represents the most affordable way to get a Max-series Apple Silicon chip (which starts at $4,099/£4,099 if you buy a MacBook Pro). It is well suited to professional video production, large AI models, 3D rendering, and other heavily multi-threaded or GPU-intensive workflows.

For most users, the Mac mini is a better value purchase. However, if your workloads demand high performance, more memory and a more powerful GPU, the Mac Studio is the better choice. 

Mac mini vs MacBook Neo: Which is better value?

Thomas Armbrüster

Before the introduction of the MacBook Neo, the Mac mini was Apple’s least expensive Mac. That is no longer the case – particularly now Apple has raised the price of the entry-level Mac mini from $599/£599 to $899/£899.

The MacBook Neo is now Apple’s most affordable Mac, starting at $699/£699. It is designed as an entry-level Mac and is powered by the A18 Pro chip originally used for the iPhone 16 Pro and only offers 8GB memory. The focus is on portability, battery life, and affordability rather than performance.

The Mac mini, by contrast, remains Apple’s best-value desktop Mac for users who already own a monitor, keyboard, and mouse. Thanks to its M6 and M5 Pro chips, active cooling system, and greater performance, it is better suited to demanding workloads such as coding, creative applications, multitasking, and local AI development.

Where to buy a Mac mini

If you’re looking to buy a Mac mini, you can choose between Apple, third-party retailers and refurbished outlets.

Apple: You can buy a Mac mini directly from the Apple Store online or at an Apple retail store.

Apple Education Store: Apple also offers discounted education pricing for eligible students and educators via its Education Store. For example, the $899 M6 Mac mini costs $799 with education pricing.

Third-Party Resellers: It’s worth checking third-party retailers as well as Apple, as stores such as Amazon and B&H frequently discount Macs. Authorized resellers and major retailers often sell the Mac mini at less than Apple’s list price.

In the U.S., retailers include:

  • Amazon
  • Best Buy
  • B&H Photo Video
  • Costco
  • Adorama
  • DataVision

In the U.K., retailers include:

  • Amazon
  • Argos
  • Currys
  • John Lewis
  • AO
  • Ebuyer
  • Laptops Direct

The U.K. also has Apple Premium Resellers including KRCS, iStore, Select, Albion and Jigsaw.

Should you buy a refurbished Mac mini?

A refurbished Mac mini can be an excellent way to save money, particularly if you don’t need the latest model. Discounts can be significant, although the exact saving depends on the model, configuration and seller.

The best place to start is Apple’s Refurbished Store. Apple’s refurbished Macs are fully tested, cleaned and inspected, and come with a one-year limited warranty, 90 days of technical support and eligibility for AppleCare. They are also supplied with the appropriate accessories and repackaged in a new box.

Earlier in 2026, we saw refurbished M4 Mac mini models discounted by around $90/£90, with savings also available on the M4 Pro version. However, as of September 2026, refurbished Mac mini stock is very limited. M4 models are currently unavailable, and it may be some time before the new M6 and M5 Pro models start appearing in Apple’s refurbished store.

Availability is one of the main drawbacks of buying refurbished. Stock depends on returns and trade-ins, so you may not find the exact memory or storage configuration you want. More models may become available as owners upgrade to the latest Mac minis and older machines make their way to refurbishers.

You should also be careful when buying from third-party sellers. Refurbishment standards and warranties can vary, and marketplaces may contain much older Intel-based Mac minis. We generally wouldn’t recommend those models now unless the price is exceptionally low, as Apple silicon Mac minis offer much better performance and will receive software support for longer.

We’ve found Amazon particularly worth checking carefully. Refurbished stock can be dominated by Mac minis from 2020 or earlier, and we’ve even seen discontinued configurations listed for more than their original selling price. Always check the model year, specification and price of an equivalent new Mac before buying.

Buying refurbished is generally safer than buying second hand from a private seller. A reputable refurbished Mac should have been inspected and tested and will usually include a warranty and returns policy. A privately sold Mac may offer neither, and there is also a risk of Activation Lock if the previous owner hasn’t properly removed the Mac from their Apple Account.

Where to buy a refurbished Mac mini

U.S.: Amazon, Back Market, Best Buy, GainSaver, Mac of All Trades and Refurb.me.

U.K.: Affordable Mac, Amazon, Back Market, Hoxton Macs, MacFinder, Mac4Sale and MusicMagpie.

Read our guide to the pros and cons of buying refurbished Macs. We also have recommendations of the best places to buy a refurbished Mac.

title: What kills Schrödinger’s cat? Gravity may not be the answer
description: Physicists have put a decades-old idea about why the strange rules of quantum mechanics disappear in our everyday world to one of its toughest experimental tests yet. Deep beneath Italy’s Gran Sasso mountain, researchers searched for an extremely faint radiation signal predicted by a theory suggesting that tiny fluctuations in spacetime, caused by gravity, gradually destroy quantum superpositions. After 62 days of measurements with a highly shielded germanium detector, they found no such signal.

title: How Can Thin Brick Support High-Performance Buildings?
description: Masonry is often perceived through its weight, depth, texture, and sense of permanence. Yet these physical qualities also have several implications for the performance of a building envelope. From the thickness of the mortar joint to the weight of the material, every masonry decision is connected to considerations of durability, stability, and long-term performance, while preserving the material character associated with solidity and permanence. At Summer Street Apartments, thin brick offered a way to retain these qualities while accommodating the insulation and envelope requirements of an all-electric, net-zero energy building. Just as importantly, it helped give the project the residential character the architects were looking for.

title: "The Homes of Tomorrow Are Already Built": European Citizens' Initiative for the Right to Housing Opens Signature Collection
description: "Right to Housing! Now and Forever" is an official European Citizens' Initiative (ECI) to demand affordable, sustainable, and fair housing across the European Union. The ECI is a governance tool that allows citizens to propose new laws for the European Commission to consider. Initiatives must be organized by a group of at least seven EU citizens living in seven different countries and must gather 1 million valid signatures within one year of receiving official approval. The signature collection for "Right to Housing! Now and Forever" launched on September 14, 2026, and aims to collect 1.2 million signatures across the EU to require the European Commission to formally respond to and address the proposal. The project builds on the HouseEurope! European Citizens' Initiative, which focused strictly on building renovation and closed unsuccessfully on January 31, 2026. This new proposal, put forward by a broader coalition, encompasses not only renovation but also financing tools and measures to ensure access.
